senses.gloss: m. = אִיהוּ (mostly after an open syllable to avoid a hiatus, or after ן) he, himself; it, it is.
units: <cite ref="Bava Kamma 114b:29">B. Kam. 114ᵇ</cite> <he>דילמא … והוא נ׳ קא מפיק שמא</he> perhaps he sold them, and he himself spread the report (that they had been stolen).
<cite ref="Berakhot 58b:11">Ber. 58ᵇ</cite> <he>לא ידענא מאי נ׳</he> I do not know what it is (its nature).
<cite ref="Taanit 24a:1">Taan. 24ᵃ</cite> <he>אנא נ׳</he> (differ. in Ms. M.) I am he (of whom you are speaking).
Pes. 104ᵃ, a. e. מאן נ׳ בנן וכ׳ (Ms. M. נינהו, v. Rabb. D. S. a. l. note) who is (are) meant by ‘the son of saints’?; a. fr.—Fem. נִיהִי.

<cite ref="Chullin 38a:2">Ḥull. 38ᵃ</cite> <he>מאי נ׳ דברים וכ׳</he> what are the movements indicating the agony of death? <cite ref="Chullin 79a:4">Ib. 79ᵃ</cite> <he>כולהו חדא מינא נ׳</he> they all belong to the same species.
B. Mets. 24ᵇ רובה ישראל ננהו the majority are Jews; a. fr.—With suffixes: נִיהֲלִי, נִיהֲלָךְ, נִיהֲלֵיה &c. (to) myself, thyself, himself &c.
Ḥull. 59ᵇ בעינא דמחזית ליה ניהלי (Rashi דמחזית ניהליה) I want thee to show him to me (Rashi: to make him visible).
<cite ref="Chullin 142a:1">Ib. 142ᵃ</cite> <he>והדר לקנינהו נ׳</he> and then let him transfer them to thyself.
Ber. 54ᵇ בריך רחמנא דיהבך נִיהֲלָן וכ׳ blessed be the Merciful who returned thee to us and not to the dust.
<cite ref="Nedarim 41a">Ned. 41ᵃ</cite>; <cite ref="Eruvin 10a">Erub. 10ᵃ</cite>, a. fr. <he>את אמרת ניהלן וכ׳</he> thou didst cite it to ourselves &c.
<cite ref="Ketubot 92a:7">Keth. 92ᵃ</cite> <he>מגבי להו נִיהֲלַיְיהוּ ארעא</he> he will give land in payment to the very claimants, and then seize it from them; a. fr.
